name: Atorvastatin
route_note: oral tablet once daily, any time of day
owner: generic (many); Lipitor brand held by Viatris (Pfizer in some markets)

discovery.note: A fully synthetic statin with a pyrrole core; Pfizer co-marketed it and acquired Warner-Lambert in 2000.

tagline: Potent synthetic statin and the best-selling drug in pharmaceutical history
summary: Atorvastatin is a high-potency synthetic statin that lowers LDL cholesterol by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase. It is used to reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people with or at risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and to treat hypercholesterolaemia.
mechanism: Atorvastatin competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis, mainly in the liver.

Falling intracellular cholesterol activates SREBP-2, which increases expression of LDL receptors on hepatocytes. More receptors clear more LDL particles from the blood, lowering LDL cholesterol; statins also modestly lower triglycerides and raise HDL.
Its long-lived active metabolites contribute to a prolonged effect, allowing dosing at any time of day.
uses: Primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular events
Heterozygous and homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (including children ≥10 years)

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Bruce Roth synthesises the compound at Parke-Davis.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Lipitor, co-promoted by Warner-Lambert and Pfizer.

history.title: Pfizer acquisition
history.detail: Pfizer acquires Warner-Lambert, largely to obtain Lipitor.

history.title: ASCOT-LLA
history.detail: Atorvastatin reduces coronary events in hypertensive patients with average cholesterol.

history.title: TNT
history.detail: High-dose atorvastatin beats low dose in stable coronary disease.

history.title: SPARCL
history.detail: Atorvastatin reduces recurrent stroke after stroke or TIA.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic atorvastatin launches in the US in November.

history.title: Viatris
history.detail: Lipitor moves to Viatris, formed from Pfizer's Upjohn unit and Mylan.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 to active ortho- and para-hydroxylated metabolites

facts: Lipitor is widely reported as the top-selling drug of all time by cumulative revenue.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and grapefruit juice in large amounts increase exposure.
